chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man to whom I had advanced dirhams for food; then when the time for my food came due upon him, he sent dirhams to me and said: 'Buy food for yourself and take your due in full.'
So he عليه السلام said: 'I hold that you should assign that to someone other than yourself, and stand with him until you receive what is yours, and do not you yourself undertake its purchase.'

key_terms.أَسْلَفْتُهُ: I advanced him payment in a salam-type transaction
key_terms.تُوَلِّيَ: to appoint or assign someone to handle a matter
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver coin currency used for payment
key_terms.طَعَامٍ: food commodity owed in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor personally buy food with money sent by a debtor to settle an advance sale debt?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal issue involving advance payment for food and the settlement of the creditor's due. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام instructs that the creditor should not personally purchase the replacement food with the debtor's money, but should appoint another person and witness the receipt of what is owed.
